newsitem.title: CHINA: China tells Xinjiang troops to be on high alert.
newsitem.headline: China tells Xinjiang troops to be on high alert.

text.p: China has told its troops in its restive mainly Moslem Xinjiang region to maintain a high state of alert just days before the British colony of Hong Kong is to return to Chinese rule, the People's Daily newspaper said on Wednesday.

"Xinjiang... is a large area with a long border and soldiers there must maintain a high state of alert," the newspaper quoted Minister of Defence Chi Haotian as saying on a recent visit to the farflung northwestern region.

On a tour of the region from June 21-23, Chi called on soldiers in Xinjiang to step up their drills and ensure the safety and stability of the mainly Moslem region, which has been rocked repeatedly by separatist violence in recent years.

China's rulers are keen to ensure nothing taints the July 1 handover of Hong Kong and have boosted security and police patrols in the run-up to the event that Beijing has called one of China's most important moments of the year, if not the century.
Violence in Xinjiang, which is populated mostly by members of the mainly Moslem Uighur ethnic minority, has previously marred occasions Beijing has tried to present as solemn and dignified.

In late February, a string of homemade bus bombs blew up in the regional capital of Urumqi, killing at least nine in an attack that coincided with funeral rites in Beijing for the late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
